verdict.rationale: Anytype documents custom Types as blueprints for objects. Properties are stored on objects, and Queries retrieve objects by criteria, which covers the core of typed organization and retrieval. However, the evidence never explicitly documents tags or the kinds of property data types available. missing for 10: explicit documentation of tags/multi-select tagging, property data types (date/select/number etc.), independent hands-on corroboration of consistent property-based retrieval

support.subject: As a power-user, I can attach typed properties and tags to notes and use them consistently for organization and retrieval

citations.quote: Anytype comes with built-in Types, but you can create your own custom Types to match your needs.
It's a blueprint that defines what the Object is. Notes, Tasks, Books, People, Images—these are all Types.
Anytype fetches metadata from the URL — title, description, preview image, and favicon — and stores them as Properties on the Object.
Rather than manually curating a list of things you're looking for, you define the criteria and the Query assembles the result for you as a View.
Learn how to query, retrieve, and update spaces, objects, properties, types, and templates to build powerful extensions.
